title: Count matches without mutating state from a lambda

blocks.text: A lambda cannot write to a local variable of its method, so `items.forEach(item -> count++)` does not compile. The tempting way around it is to keep the count somewhere the lambda *can* write. The page's better advice is to avoid the side effect and let a stream do the counting.

Write `MatchCounter.countMatches(List<String> items, Predicate<String> condition)`, an instance method that returns how many items the condition accepts. The list may contain `null` items: they are never counted, and the condition is never called with `null`.
The same `MatchCounter` may be asked many times; each answer must stand on its own.

cases.says: It counts the items the condition accepts.
Null items are skipped and never handed to the condition.
A second call on the same counter counts from zero again; no count is kept between calls.
The condition is never called with null, not even inside a try that would swallow its failure.

concepts: Mutating shared state from a lambda to get around effectively final is a bug waiting to happen; let a stream compute the result instead.
Null items and empty collections are handled in the pipeline before a lambda sees them.
